source: Owner (Taren), 2026-11-06, choosing from the clickable layout mockup (rounds 1 to 4) in the Claude Code session that planned this step. Belongs in Shop Settings once that module exists. Entries listed under "proposed" were mockup defaults the owner used without changing; they are not yet confirmed. min_run_length (9") was approved by the owner on 2026-11-07, for base and upper pieces.

proposed.default_run_kind: PROPOSED (2026-11-06): a run made by tapping or dragging along a wall starts as base + upper, as in the mockup.
proposed.island_run_kind: PROPOSED (2026-11-06): an island's run starts as base only.
proposed.run_depths: PROPOSED (2026-11-06): base 24", upper-only 12", and the 13" band that shows uppers on a base + upper run; mockup defaults.
proposed.island_start_size: PROPOSED (2026-11-06): the "Add island" button makes a 72" x 36" island, as in the mockup.
proposed.appliance_flags: PROPOSED (2026-11-06): a fridge or wall oven is kept out from in front of a window; a wall oven dropped on a bare wall gets an all-pantry run. Mockup behaviour the owner did not object to.

decided.sink_run: Owner, 2026-11-12 (after the Fake Design kitchen): "Why didn't the uppers around the sink window go to the window? They stop very short." A sink (and so its dishwasher) dropped on a bare wall used to get a base-only run, so no uppers were drawn either side of the window over it. Its run now starts as base + upper, like any other kitchen run; uppers still skip the window itself.

over_cooking.source: Owner, 2026-11-09 (chat): the designer chooses what goes over a range or cooktop: a cabinet, an appliance hood or a millwork hood, on the appliance. A new one starts as an appliance hood (as ranges and cooktops always had, 2026-11-06).

room_sets.source: Owner, 2026-11-09 (chat): bathroom-type rooms offer a toilet (30" clear space), vanity sink (20" bowl), double vanity sink (60"), tub (60") and shower (48"); their runs start base-only, 21" deep for the catalog's 20 3/4" vanities. A run of "run_when_alone": null means the fixture stands on the floor, not on a cabinet run. Which rooms are bathrooms is the intake's own room-type grouping ("bath"); other room types use the kitchen set until the owner says otherwise (PROPOSED).
